title: Aud lease and CUPE 68 agreements approved
subtitle: Council appointments deferred a week; remembrance days for the Québec City Mosque attack and the Holocaust acknowledged.
overview: Council met in a short special meeting and then went into a closed session. Afterward, it approved a lease agreement for services at the Kitchener Memorial Auditorium Complex (The Aud) {{vote:m3}}. The General Manager of Community Services and Deputy CAO can now sign it, subject to the City Solicitor's satisfaction. The minutes do not publicly give the lease terms.

Council also approved the terms of two Memoranda of Settlement dated December 17, 2025. They set the 2026-2029 collective agreements with CUPE 68 Civics and CUPE 68 Mechanics {{vote:m4}}. The Mayor and Clerk may sign the documents. These agreements set employment terms for city staff over the next four years.

Council deferred its appointments of members to boards and committees to the February 2, 2026 special meeting so all members can attend in person {{vote:m1}}. The Mayor opened the meeting by marking the National Day of Remembrance of the Québec City Mosque Attack and Action against Islamophobia, and International Holocaust Remembrance Day. There were no delegations.

decisions.detail: Council authorized the General Manager, Community Services and Deputy CAO to approve and execute a lease for services at the Kitchener Memorial Auditorium Complex, on terms discussed in closed session and to the City Solicitor's satisfaction.
Council approved the Memoranda of Settlement for the 2026-2029 collective agreements with CUPE 68 Civics and CUPE 68 Mechanics and authorized the Mayor and Clerk to sign them.
Council deferred its member appointments to boards and committees to the February 2, 2026 special meeting so all members can attend in person.

debate: No delegations registered to speak, and the transcript records no debate on the motions; each was put to a vote after the Mayor called for movers and seconders.
The deferral of council appointments was proposed so the item could be considered at the next week's council meeting; the minutes give the reason as allowing all members to attend in person.
The Mayor's remarks on the two remembrance days called for confronting hatred and discrimination, and invited people to wear a green square in memory of the Québec City attack victims.
